svg.text: Boundary-position consistency · raw observations, cross-species difference and mapping status
For each comparable boundary, where does each species place it relative to the nearest domain edge, how far apart are those placements, and how well supported is the comparison?
A · raw signed distance per species (aa)

Panel A — upper lane: H. sapiens · lower lane: P. troglodytes · lower lane: G. gorilla gorilla · lower lane: P. abelii · lower lane: M. mulatta · lower lane: C. jacchus · lower lane: M. musculus · lower lane: R. norvegicus · lower lane: O. cuniculus · lower lane: F. catus · lower lane: B. taurus · lower lane: S. scrofa · lower lane: E. caballus · lower lane: O. aries · lower lane: M. domestica · lower lane: O. anatinus · lower lane: G. gallus · lower lane: M. gallopavo · lower lane: T. guttata · lower lane: A. carolinensis · lower lane: A. mississippiensis · lower lane: C. picta bellii · lower lane: X. tropicalis · lower lane: A. mexicanum · lower lane: D. rerio · lower lane: O. latipes · lower lane: G. aculeatus · lower lane: T. rubripes · lower lane: O. niloticus

Panel A: open marker = distance to a domain start edge, filled = end edge; solid connector = supported mapping, dotted = tentative. Panel C: filled square = all species agree on the boundary class; bar = mapping confidence; text = species observed / analysed.
A small difference is evidence of a consistent boundary position, not of evolutionary conservation.
